question: Before we let an AI agent into our files and email, what should it be allowed to see?
reflection: Careful limits on what our tools can reach let us enjoy their help while keeping our private lives in our own hands.

sources.subject: image-blaster turns one photo into a 3D world in 5 min
China's AI resellers + Apple tightens Mac access

one_line: Access is the theme of the day: Apple tightens what agents can reach on a Mac, while gray markets route around limits on US AI models and chips.

top_stories.title: Apple raises the bar for agents reading your files
top_stories.what: Apple says granting an app full access to files, mail and messages on a Mac will need a very explicit user action, because agents can now act across the whole computer.
top_stories.why: How people grant permissions to agents is a consent and trust question that behavioural design can improve.

top_stories.title: A gray market for US AI models in China
top_stories.what: Thousands of small resellers reportedly sell pooled access to Claude and other US models in China, some used to train rival models by imitation, while Anthropic bans suspicious accounts.
top_stories.why: Data sent through such resellers can be exposed, a reminder to check exactly where any AI service sends sensitive research data.

top_stories.title: European open model with a very long memory
top_stories.what: Aleph Alpha released Kolibri-1, an open-weight model under a permissive licence that switches on only a small part of itself per word and reportedly reads up to a million tokens.
top_stories.why: Open models that run on your own servers suit organisations that must keep data local.

saudi_lens.text: Export-control enforcement against chip smuggling routes through Asia matters for Saudi Arabia, which needs to show strict controls to keep access to advanced US chips.

idea.title: Agent permission audit kit
idea.pitch: A short workshop and checklist that helps teams list what each AI agent can reach, the worst realistic failure, and which human approvals must stay.
idea.first_step: Draft a one-page permission table with Allow, Limit and Deny columns and test it on one tool your team uses.

idea_kids.title: Who gets the key? story book
idea_kids.pitch: A picture book where a family robot asks for keys to different rooms, and children decide which rooms it really needs to enter and why.
idea_kids.first_step: Write a short draft with six rooms and one question per page.

terms.definition: Training one model to copy the answers of another, often a stronger one.
Government rules that limit which products, such as advanced chips, can be sold to certain countries.
A model design where only a small set of specialist parts switch on for each request, so a huge model runs at the cost of a smaller one.

concepts.summary: Restricted chips and model access keep leaking through resellers and third countries.
Labs fight unauthorised use of their models to train rivals.
Operating systems and teams rethink what agents may access on a computer.
